Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 1) According to the biomedical concept, health means:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Biomedical concept considers health mainly as absence of disease. It gives less importance to social, psychological and environmental factors.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 2) The ecological concept of health emphasizes:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Ecological concept explains health and disease as adjustment or maladjustment between human beings and their environment.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 3) The psychosocial concept considers health as:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Psychosocial concept says health is both biological and social. It adds social and psychological dimensions beyond disease absence.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 4) The holistic concept of health is best described as:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Holistic concept combines biomedical, ecological and psychosocial views. It gives a more complete understanding of health.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 5) As per WHO definition, the three specific dimensions of health are physical, mental and:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: WHO definition specifically mentions physical, mental and social well-being. These are the three classical dimensions of health.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 6) Physical dimension of health mainly indicates:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Physical health refers to bodily structure, function, fitness and ability to perform daily activities without undue fatigue.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 7) Mental health mainly refers to:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Mental health includes emotional stability, clear thinking, coping ability and balanced behaviour in daily life.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 8) Social health refers to:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option3: Ability to maintain satisfactory relationship with others
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Social health means ability to live harmoniously with others and perform social roles properly.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 9) Physical Quality of Life Index includes infant mortality rate, life expectancy at age one and:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: PQLI has three components: infant mortality rate, life expectancy at age one and literacy.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 10) PQLI does not directly include:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: PQLI measures quality of life using IMR, life expectancy at age one and literacy. Income is not a direct component.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 11) Human Development Index includes longevity, knowledge and:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: HDI includes longevity, knowledge and income. Longevity is measured by life expectancy at birth.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 12) Longevity in HDI is measured by:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: In HDI, longevity means life expectancy at birth. It reflects survival and general health status.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 13) Knowledge component of HDI includes adult literacy rate and:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: HDI knowledge component includes adult literacy and mean years of schooling. It reflects educational achievement.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 14) Income component of HDI is represented by:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: In the uploaded note, income component of HDI is represented by GDP in US dollar.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 15) Illness is best defined as:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option1: Individual’s perception and behaviour in response to disease
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Illness is the person’s own perception and response to disease. It may exist even when objective disease is not obvious.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 16) Sickness means:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option2: Social dysfunction of a diseased person
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Sickness is the social role or dysfunction caused by disease. It affects ability to perform normal social duties.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 17) A patient feels weak and unwell, but all tests are normal. This is closest to:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Illness is subjective feeling and behaviour in response to perceived disease. It does not always need objective test abnormality.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 18) A worker cannot attend office due to tuberculosis. This is closest to:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Sickness means social dysfunction due to disease. Inability to perform social or occupational role is the key point.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 19) The first stage of the disease cycle is:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Incubation period starts after the disease agent enters the host. No clinical signs or symptoms are present.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 20) During incubation period:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option3: No clinical sign or symptom appears
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: In incubation period, the agent is present in the host but clinical manifestations are absent.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 21) Vague symptoms without specific diagnostic signs occur in:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Prodromal period produces vague, non-specific symptoms. Clear diagnostic features are still absent.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 22) Clear-cut specific signs and symptoms appear during:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Fastigium is the stage when specific signs and symptoms appear. The disease can be clinically diagnosed at this stage.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 23) The stage where body defence begins to take upper hand is:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: In defervescence, the patient begins to improve as body defence mechanisms start dominating over disease process.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 24) Recovery with weakness while still harboring disease agent is:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: In convalescence, the patient recovers clinically but remains weak and may still harbor disease agents.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 25) Complete recovery from disease is called:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Defection is the final stage where the individual completely recovers from the disease.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 26) In the iceberg phenomenon, the visible tip represents:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: The visible tip of the iceberg represents apparent clinical cases. These are the cases usually seen by physicians.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 27) The submerged part of iceberg phenomenon represents:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option2: Subclinical, latent, undiagnosed cases and carriers
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: The submerged part represents hidden morbidity. It includes latent cases, subclinical cases, undiagnosed cases and carriers.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 28) The waterline in iceberg phenomenon represents:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option4: Demarcation between apparent and inapparent disease
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: The waterline separates visible clinical cases from hidden inapparent disease in the community.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 29) In iceberg phenomenon, approximately visible part above water is:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: The uploaded file states that only about 1/12th of iceberg is visible above water. This represents apparent disease.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 30) Iceberg phenomenon is classically applicable to:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Hypertension has many undiagnosed and subclinical cases in the community. Therefore, hidden morbidity far exceeds known morbidity.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 31) Another example of iceberg phenomenon is:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Leprosy may have many hidden, undetected and subclinical cases. Therefore, it fits the iceberg phenomenon.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 32) In iceberg phenomenon, unknown morbidity is usually:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: In diseases showing iceberg phenomenon, hidden or unknown morbidity far exceeds known morbidity.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 33) Diabetes mellitus is an example of iceberg phenomenon because:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Diabetes may remain asymptomatic for long periods. Many people are detected only by screening or complications.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 34) Disease means:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option1: Objective pathological process in the body
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Disease is an objective abnormality of body structure or function. It may be detected clinically, pathologically or by investigation.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 35) A person may have disease without illness when:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option1: He has subclinical disease but feels normal
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option3: He has symptoms but no pathology
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Disease can be present without subjective feeling of illness. Subclinical hypertension or diabetes may be detected by screening while the person feels normal.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 36) A person may have illness without demonstrable disease when:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option1: He has malaria parasite in blood
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option3: He feels unwell but no objective abnormality is found
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Illness is subjective perception. A person may feel sick even when clinical examination and investigations do not show definite disease.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 37) The concept that “health is a means to socially and economically productive life” is closest to:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Functional concept views health as the ability to function effectively in society. It focuses on performance of social and economic roles, not merely absence of disease. It is useful in public health because it connects health with productivity and daily living.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 38) Positive health means:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option1: Presence of mild disease with treatment
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option2: Health only as absence of disease
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option3: Perfect functioning of body and mind with social adjustment
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Positive health is more than absence of disease. It implies optimum physical, mental and social functioning. It is an ideal state where a person can live productively and adjust well with society and environment.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 39) Spectrum of health usually extends from:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Health and disease are not fixed separate states. They exist on a continuum ranging from positive health to disease, disability and death. This concept helps explain why preventive, curative and rehabilitative measures are all needed.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 40) The natural history of disease refers to:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Natural history of disease means the course of disease from beginning to final outcome without intervention. It includes prepathogenesis and pathogenesis phases. Knowledge of natural history helps in planning prevention at different levels.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 41) The prepathogenesis phase of disease occurs:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option4: Before disease process starts in man
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Prepathogenesis phase occurs before the disease process begins in the human host. Agent, host and environmental factors interact during this phase. Primary prevention is mainly applied here to prevent disease occurrence.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 42) The pathogenesis phase begins when:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option4: Agent enters the host and disease process starts
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Pathogenesis phase starts when the disease agent enters the host and disease process begins. It may remain subclinical initially before signs and symptoms appear. Screening and early diagnosis are useful during early pathogenesis.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 43) In the natural history of disease, disability usually occurs:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Disability may occur when disease progresses or complications develop. It is usually a later outcome of disease. Rehabilitation aims to reduce disability and restore maximum possible function.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 44) The agent-host-environment model is also called:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: The epidemiological triad includes agent, host and environment. Disease occurs when interaction among these three favours disease development. It is a basic model for understanding communicable disease causation.

Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.question: 45) The best statement about health is:
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option2: Health is a dynamic state influenced by biological, social and environmental factors
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.option4: Health is only absence of disease
Concept of health,disease, dimensions,PQ.exp: Modern public health views health as dynamic and multidimensional. It includes biological, psychological, social and environmental influences. This is broader than the biomedical view, which limits health to absence of disease.
